title: VESPER External Observation Ingress
description: REM-008. INV-AUTO-4 makes this a PRODUCTION architectural requirement, not test scaffolding: the world model must be writable by observation sources external to the decision loop, through an authenticated, provenance-carrying ingress. Without it, A-029 part 3 would be testing the harness rather than the product -- an external controller must be able to change the world at a time drawn outside the system, and VESPER must notice. Authority: SR-020, SR-028, SR-029, SR-036, SR-040, SR-058; REM-001, REM-008, REM-011; INV-AUTO-4.

node_id.description: ADR-007 D1: a key fingerprint, enrolled through the owner-confirmed path. An unenrolled source cannot write an observation, so this ingress is not an open door onto the world model.

trust_zone.description: A sensor_node is typically Z2: it MAY render and observe; it may NOT hold state, issue commands, or receive secrets (INV-TRUST-1). The A-029 synthetic observer is enrolled exactly this way, by the production path.

session_ref.description: ADR-007 D4: writes carry the session established by mutual challenge-response. A bearer token with a long life would make this ingress forgeable.

value.description: Any JSON value, or the literal string 'UNKNOWN'. UNKNOWN is a representable value, not an absence -- REM-001 §4.5.

valid_until.description: Every observation declares a TTL. On expiry the fact becomes UNKNOWN -- never 'last known value' (INV-COORD-2). A stale fact presented as current is a guess, and RB-002 forbids guessing.

admission.description: DF-SUPERSEDE runs on every ingress write: a write with observed_at_hlc <= current is REJECTED and the rejection is EMITTED (INV-COORD-1). Rejections are recorded so a silently-dropped observation is distinguishable from one that never arrived.

$comment: STRUCTURALLY REQUIRED, NOT OPTIONAL. If an implementation ships without this ingress, A-029 part 3 cannot run at all: there is no way for an external controller to change the world at an unpredictable time, and the only remaining way to make a trigger fire is a clock -- which is the C1 cron build the whole gate exists to fail. EXCLUDED BY DESIGN: any test-only or debug-only variant of this endpoint. A production requirement satisfied by a test fixture is deleted during cleanup and then argued away.
